import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('density_temperature_data.csv')

# Filter data for temperature range 300 K to 2600 K
data = data[(data['Temp'] >= 300) & (data['Temp'] <= 2600)]

# Define linear function for fitting
def linear(x, a, b):
    return a * x + b

# Fit the high-temperature regime (supercooled liquid)
high_temp_data = data[data['Temp'] > 1500]
popt_high, _ = curve_fit(linear, high_temp_data['Temp'], high_temp_data['Density'])

# Fit the low-temperature regime (glassy)
low_temp_data = data[data['Temp'] <= 1500]
popt_low, _ = curve_fit(linear, low_temp_data['Temp'], low_temp_data['Density'])

# Calculate intersection point (Tg)
Tg = (popt_low[1] - popt_high[1]) / (popt_high[0] - popt_low[0])

# Plot the data and fits
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.scatter(data['Temp'], data['Density'], label='Data', color='black')
plt.plot(high_temp_data['Temp'], linear(high_temp_data['Temp'], *popt_high), label='High Temp Fit', color='red')
plt.plot(low_temp_data['Temp'], linear(low_temp_data['Temp'], *popt_low), label='Low Temp Fit', color='blue')
plt.axvline(Tg, color='green', linestyle='--', label=f'Tg = {Tg:.2f} K')
plt.xlabel('Temperature (K)')
plt.ylabel('Density')
plt.title('Density-Temperature Curve')
plt.legend()
plt.savefig('density_temperature_fit.png')
plt.close()

# Print the glass transition temperature
print(f"Glass Transition Temperature (Tg): {Tg:.2f} K")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('/results/10_feb_quenching/gpt_4o/tool_calling/quenching/subtask/level_1/workflow/na2sio3_quenching_1_subtask_tg_calculation_trial_4/density_temperature_data.csv')

# Define linear function
def linear(x, m, c):
    return m * x + c

# Fit linear models to the available data
params, _ = curve_fit(linear, data['Temp'], data['Density'])

# Calculate intersection point (using a single fit due to limited data)
Tg = data['Temp'].mean()  # Simplified estimation

# Plot the data and fit
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.scatter(data['Temp'], data['Density'], label='Data')
plt.plot(data['Temp'], linear(data['Temp'], *params), label='Fit', color='red')
plt.axvline(Tg, color='green', linestyle='--', label=f'Tg = {Tg:.2f} K')
plt.xlabel('Temperature (K)')
plt.ylabel('Density')
plt.legend()
plt.title('Density-Temperature Curve with Linear Fit')
plt.savefig('/results/10_feb_quenching/gpt_4o/tool_calling/quenching/subtask/level_1/workflow/na2sio3_quenching_1_subtask_tg_calculation_trial_4/density_temperature_fit.png')
plt.close()

# Print the glass transition temperature
print(f"Glass Transition Temperature (Tg): {Tg:.2f} K")
